hypotheses.justification:
The proof uses `hv` in exactly one place: to build `IndivData`, whose field `vLt` gives `iLt : p.pos[v]! < n` (via `hp.posLt`). Everything after that (`individualize_cst_getElemD`, `cst_eq`) needs only `i := p.pos[v]! < n`. That fact holds without `hv` whenever the goal is not vacuous.

After `intro k hk hstart` we have `k < n`, so `0 < n`. If `n = 0`, `Refines 0 _ _` is vacuous.

There are two cases for `v`:
- If `v < n`, `hp.posLt v` gives `p.pos[v]! < n`.
- If `v ≥ n`, then `p.pos.size = n ≤ v` by `hp.posSize`. The access `p.pos[v]!` is out of bounds, so it returns `default = 0`, and `0 < n`.

With `hi : p.pos[v]! < n`, set `c := p.cst[i]!` and `ec := p.cen[i]!`. Rewrite with `individualize_cst_eq` (true by `rfl`, no hypotheses). Then apply `setCstFrom_getElemD`. Its size side condition is `ec ≤ p.cst.size`, which follows from `hp.cenLe i hi` and `hp.cstSize`. Its fuel condition `ec ≤ (c+1) + (ec-(c+1))` holds by `omega`. The goal becomes `(if c+1 ≤ k ∧ k < ec then c+1 else p.cst[k]!) = k`.
- In the `else` branch, `hstart` closes the goal.
- In the `then` branch, `hp.cellCst i hi k` (using `c ≤ k < ec`) gives `p.cst[k]! = c`. With `hstart` this gives `k = c`, which contradicts `c+1 ≤ k` (`omega`).

In short, this is the existing proof with `IndivData.cst_eq` replaced by `hp.cellCst` on the index `p.pos[v]!`, whose bound comes from the case split above instead of from `hv`. Concretely, for `v ≥ n` individualization works on position 0's cell. It still only splits that cell, so no cell start is lost.
